Expose `reduction_dtype` consistently for NCCL tensor-parallel sums: native (`None`), FP16, BF16, FP32 or FP64, retaining the original result dtype. Cover Linear and LayerNormMLP forward, ops.Linear, and sequence-parallel reduce-scatter. LayerNormLinear rejects row parallelism in this version, so its option controls the column-parallel input-gradient reduction before normalization backward.

Preserve the option through compile eager fallback, validate singleton groups, and copy asynchronous results back on `wait()`. Reject module Userbuffers/symmetric reductions that cannot honor the setting; ops Userbuffers forward fusion leaves explicit dtype selection on the standard collective path.

Validation on 2 × H20, Torch 2.7.0+cu128, CUDA 12.8, cuDNN 9.7.1 and NCCL 2.26.2:

- 256 two-rank tests passed per rank, including all supported dtypes, async identity/wait, sequence parallelism, independent FP64 numerical references, fallback and fusion. Three new-feature cases fail on the reviewed head as expected.
- Original affected sanity matrix: 7,668 passed, 8,964 skipped and 4,403 deselected. L0 license and pre-commit passed. Python lint reports the same existing E1135 on `pools` in both sources, with no new diagnostics.

Every arm matches the independent native-dtype TE reference's prefill logits and tokens exactly; each case records 8,960 real reductions per rank. Test checkpoint files were cleaned after completion.

Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Medium impact]** The latest change appears safe to merge and fixes the worker-crash reporting issue.

Summary

Extends `reduction_dtype` across tensor-parallel modules and ops while keeping the original result dtype. - Tensor-parallel sums can use a chosen communication dtype and keep their original output dtype. - PyTorch modules can choose the dtype used for tensor-parallel sums. - `ops.Linear` can choose the dtype used for row-parallel reductions.

Diagram

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart LR A[Original tensor] --> B{Explicit reduction dtype?} B -->|No| C[Native collective] B -->|Yes| D[Cast to selected dtype] D --> E[NCCL sum] E --> F[Copy back in original dtype] F --> G[Return result] C --> G ``` Reviews (5) · Last reviewed commit: ["Fail the validation launcher when a rank..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/3aece45428c943dc5f51422bb65f67e08b339b9e) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

> My issue with this PR is that it introduces a new option in a very "spikey" way. For example:
>  - only Linear is covered, whereas LayerNormLinear and LayerNormMLP are not, even though they could also exercise this allreduce path.
>  - only module is covered and not ops linear variant
>  - the only accepted value for the reduction dtype is FP32. Why not accept any type there, including BF16? That way somebody experimenting with this setting would not need to completely change their model just to switch it on or off.
>  - why not add the reduce scatter option to it in addition to allreduce - this would enable the sequence parallel support.

Okay, I will have a try to expand the coverage.

The expansion is implemented in c0fda11; the current head, 6a820a9, adds the validation report and raw results.

- `Linear`, `LayerNormLinear`, `LayerNormMLP`, and `ops.Linear` accept `reduction_dtype` with native/default, FP16, BF16, FP32, and FP64 communication.
- Both all-reduce and sequence-parallel reduce-scatter are covered, with results cast back to the tensor's original dtype.
- `LayerNormLinear` applies the option to its column-parallel input-gradient reduction; this version does not support row-parallel `LayerNormLinear`.

The recorded two-H20 validation passed 256 cases per rank, including dtype combinations, sequence parallelism, async cast-back, fallback, and fusion handling. Full-checkpoint Qwen3-0.6B inference also matched the native-dtype reference for logits and generated tokens. Details, limitations, and raw results are in the [validation report](https://github.com/0z5a/TransformerEngine/blob/6a820a9f402ddf99368d829f61e3a9abe901b798/tests/pytorch/distributed/validation_reduction/TEST_RESULT_H20_REDUCTION.md).

**Fallback Drops Reduction Dtype** Under `torch.compile`, configurations that trigger the early eager fallback return before this validation. `_forward_eager_fallback` then calls `Linear.forward` without `reduction_dtype`. A row-parallel BF16 layer using an option such as `fuse_wgrad_accumulation=True` therefore performs the original BF16 reduction despite requesting `torch.float32`. Unsupported dtype values are also swallowed instead of rejected. Validate the option before the early return and preserve it through the fallback.

My issue with this PR is that it introduces a new option in a very "spikey" way. For example:
 - only Linear is covered, whereas LayerNormLinear and LayerNormMLP are not, even though they could also exercise this allreduce path.
 - only module is covered and not ops linear variant

If the other worker exits normally, `max(0, -6)` returns zero, so the validation command appears to pass. Return a nonzero status whenever either worker's exit code is nonzero. ```suggestion raise SystemExit(int(any(row["exit_code"] != 0 for row in rows))) ```

 PyTorch
 =======
 
+Tensor-parallel reduction dtype
+-------------------------------
+
+``reduction_dtype`` selects ``torch.float16``, ``torch.bfloat16``,
+``torch.float32`` or ``torch.float64`` for the NCCL sum. ``None`` preserves
+native communication. The result is cast back to the original tensor dtype;
+this does not change GEMM accumulation or retain a wider output.
+
+Pass this keyword to ``Linear.forward`` for its row-parallel output reduction
+and to ``LayerNormMLP.forward`` for its FC2 output reduction. For
+``ops.Linear``, set it in the constructor. Sequence parallelism uses the same
+option for reduce-scatter. These forward options leave backward unchanged.
+
+``LayerNormLinear`` supports column parallelism and rejects row parallelism.
+Its ``forward`` keyword selects the input-gradient reduction in backward,
+before normalization backward; its forward output is unchanged. This applies
+to both all-reduce and sequence-parallel reduce-scatter.
+
+Module Userbuffers and symmetric all-reduce do not support this option and
+raise ``ValueError``. An explicit dtype in ``ops.Linear`` prevents Userbuffers
+forward fusion from discarding the option and uses the standard collective.
+Direct ``allreduce`` and ``reduce_scatter_along_first_dim`` calls also accept
+the option; for asynchronous casts, call the returned handle's ``wait()``
+before consuming the output.
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+    # Row-parallel module: switch precision without changing the layer.
+    output = linear(input_shard, reduction_dtype=torch.float32)
+    output = linear(input_shard, reduction_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    # Column-parallel fused normalization: select input-gradient precision.
+    output = norm_linear(input, reduction_dtype=torch.float32)
+
+Modules
+-------
+
 .. autoapiclass:: transformer_engine.pytorch.Linear(in_features, out_features, **kwargs)
   :members: forward, set_tensor_parallel_group

+# Copyright (c) 2022-2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+#
+# See LICENSE for license information.
+
+"""Two-rank NCCL tests for tensor-parallel reduction dtype selection."""
+
+import os
+from importlib import import_module
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+import transformer_engine.pytorch as te
+import transformer_engine.pytorch.ops as ops
+from transformer_engine.pytorch.distributed import (
+    _AsyncHandle,
+    allreduce,
+    reduce_scatter_along_first_dim,
+)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def group():
+    if "WORLD_SIZE" not in os.environ:
+        pytest.skip("Launch two ranks with validation_reduction/launch.py")
+    assert int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"]) == 2
+    rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
+    torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
+    dist.init_process_group(
+        "nccl", init_method=f"file://{os.environ['NVTE_TEST_RDZV_PATH']}", rank=rank, world_size=2
+    )
+    yield dist.group.WORLD
+    dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+DTYPES = [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32]
+REDUCTION_DTYPES = [None, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32, torch.float64]
+
+
+def rounded_sum(inp, group, dtype):
+    inp = inp.contiguous()
+    parts = [torch.empty_like(inp) for _ in range(2)]
+    dist.all_gather(parts, inp, group=group)
+    dtype = inp.dtype if dtype is None else dtype
+    return torch.stack([part.to(dtype).double() for part in parts]).sum(0).to(dtype)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("input_dtype", DTYPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("reduction_dtype", REDUCTION_DTYPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scatter", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("async_op", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("contiguous", [False, True])
+def test_collective_dtype(group, input_dtype, reduction_dtype, scatter, async_op, contiguous):
+    torch.manual_seed(2026 + dist.get_rank(group))
+    inp = torch.randn(16, 8, device="cuda", dtype=input_dtype)
+    if not contiguous:
+        inp = inp.t().contiguous().t()
+    original = inp.clone()
+    if not contiguous and not scatter and reduction_dtype is None:
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="contiguous"):
+            allreduce(inp, group, async_op=async_op)
+        return
+    expected = rounded_sum(inp, group, reduction_dtype).to(input_dtype)
+    if scatter:
+        expected = expected.chunk(2)[dist.get_rank(group)]
+        buffer = torch.empty_like(expected)
+        out, handle = reduce_scatter_along_first_dim(
+            inp, group, async_op=async_op, output=buffer, reduction_dtype=reduction_dtype
+        )
+        assert out is buffer
+    else:
+        out, handle = allreduce(inp, group, async_op=async_op, reduction_dtype=reduction_dtype)
+        assert out is inp
+    if async_op:
+        assert handle is not None
+        handle.wait()
+        handle.wait()
+    else:
+        assert handle is None
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert out.dtype == input_dtype and out.device == inp.device
+    if scatter:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(inp, original, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def make_layer(kind, dtype, sequence_parallel, group, reduction_dtype=None):
+    if kind == "ops.Linear":
+        return ops.Linear(
+            64,
+            64,
+            bias=False,
+            dtype=dtype,
+            tensor_parallel_mode="row",
+            tensor_parallel_group=group,
+            sequence_parallel=sequence_parallel,
+            reduction_dtype=reduction_dtype,
+        )
+    kwargs = dict(
+        bias=False,
+        params_dtype=dtype,
+        tp_group=group,
+        tp_size=2,
+        sequence_parallel=sequence_parallel,
+    )
+    if kind == "Linear":
+        return te.Linear(64, 64, parallel_mode="row", **kwargs)
+    if kind == "LayerNormLinear":
+        return te.LayerNormLinear(64, 64, parallel_mode="column", **kwargs)
+    return te.LayerNormMLP(64, 128, set_parallel_mode=True, **kwargs)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["Linear", "LayerNormLinear", "LayerNormMLP", "ops.Linear"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("input_dtype", DTYPES)

**[Medium impact]** The latest change appears safe to merge and fixes the worker-crash reporting issue.

Summary

Extends `reduction_dtype` across tensor-parallel modules and ops while keeping the original result dtype. - Tensor-parallel sums can use a chosen communication dtype and keep their original output dtype. - PyTorch modules can choose the dtype used for tensor-parallel sums. - `ops.Linear` can choose the dtype used for row-parallel reductions.

>  - only Linear is covered, whereas LayerNormLinear and LayerNormMLP are not, even though they could also exercise this allreduce path.
>  - only module is covered and not ops linear variant
>  - the only accepted value for the reduction dtype is FP32. Why not accept any type there, including BF16? That way somebody experimenting with this setting would not need to completely change their model just to switch it on or off.
>  - why not add the reduce scatter option to it in addition to allreduce - this would enable the sequence parallel support.

Okay, I will have a try to expand the coverage.

The expansion is implemented in c0fda11; the current head, 6a820a9, adds the validation report and raw results.

- `Linear`, `LayerNormLinear`, `LayerNormMLP`, and `ops.Linear` accept `reduction_dtype` with native/default, FP16, BF16, FP32, and FP64 communication.
- Both all-reduce and sequence-parallel reduce-scatter are covered, with results cast back to the tensor's original dtype.
- `LayerNormLinear` applies the option to its column-parallel input-gradient reduction; this version does not support row-parallel `LayerNormLinear`.

The recorded two-H20 validation passed 256 cases per rank, including dtype combinations, sequence parallelism, async cast-back, fallback, and fusion handling. Full-checkpoint Qwen3-0.6B inference also matched the native-dtype reference for logits and generated tokens. Details, limitations, and raw results are in the [validation report](https://github.com/0z5a/TransformerEngine/blob/6a820a9f402ddf99368d829f61e3a9abe901b798/tests/pytorch/distributed/validation_reduction/TEST_RESULT_H20_REDUCTION.md).
